Use Tier 2: replace the MultVAE self-reconstruction objective with chronological next-item prediction while retaining its encoder, decoder, and recency-weighted history representation. The latest trial reached macro HR@10=0.5125, below the recorded best of 0.5363, with Electronics particularly weak at 0.375. Reconstructing items already present in the input can reward copying observed preferences without learning which unseen item follows a history.

The components to modify are data_processing_and_feature_engineering, model_design, and training_evaluation. Construct training examples exclusively from existing training sequences: choose a position after the first interaction, encode only the preceding prefix, and use the item at that position as the next-item target. Resample positions across epochs for every eligible training user, computing the existing latest-occurrence recency weights relative to each sampled prefix. Replace the weighted history-reconstruction term with full-catalog cross-entropy for that next-item target, retaining the existing variational KL term and its annealing schedule so the experiment isolates the temporal supervision change.

Keep all four category models, dataset routing, seeds, catalog definitions, and input splits unchanged. Select checkpoints using real validation HR@10 with fixed seed-42 users and 99 unique negatives, and report the macro-average across categories. Update the predictor writer to load the resulting checkpoints and use the identical history transformation and decoder forward pass used during validation; the host continues to perform held-out inference. This change directly addresses the mismatch between reconstructing observed items during training and ranking the next item during evaluation, without adding an ensemble or increasing model size.
